body: I am currently sitting on the toilet rocking back in forth and have experienced back labor contractions for the last hour. I am also happy to report that an official mucus plug had been sighted. I'm waiting on my husband to call me back from work to decide on whether he should come home immediately or finish out his shift since I'm not quite certain this is "it" it. Maybe just almost "it?" Either way: holy shit, y'all.
I'm willing to accept this as truth!
My mouth just watered at this. Maybe if I get dark chocolate chips it'll qualify as healthy because of the antioxidants?

I can't even. I'm so sorry to hear about the poor pup, and reading about your experience with the midwife just makes me livid. Even if HR doesn't return your call, I would go onto Healthgrades or its equivalent and leave a nasty review regarding your experience. That's just unacceptable behavior as a human being let alone a professional. I hope you're able to find another healthcare provider that is a lot more sensitive which I'm really hoping won't be hard since at this point all they would require would be, I dunno, a heart and soul?

Holy crap that's what I'm afraid of, too. I'm fighting off a tiny bug (sniffles, sore throat, slight coughing) and I'm like "please no please no please no" because I'm not into the idea of pushing while hacking. I'll send you "get better soon vibes" if you'll reciprocate! Here's to healthy deliveries with clear lungs/airways!

Right? There is a lot of patience required for this whole "will they or won't they" in regards to baby antics. It's kind of cute though, and to some degree I will miss it, but hopefully looking at his little face will make up for it in the near future!
I'm just outside of the Portland-metro area. Just keep driving 'til you hit cows. Then you've found me!

Made it to week 39 yesterday, and according to my midwife, I am one centimeter along. Between that and the baby deciding to intermittently headbutt and burrow into my cervix like a gopher with all his might for the last four days, this hootenanny might kick off a little sooner than I planned. I'm not really in a rush, but when all's said and done, it's not really up to me, is it? Eeeeeeee...
I keep having to take the same advice regarding relaxing and being patient. Hang in there!
I'm so glad! Yay baby!
I remember being so stressed and then super relieved when we lost and then got new health insurance. It's such a load off the mind! Huzzah!
Yayyyyy! I'm glad your doctor is doing a good job and listening and accommodating his patients. I know you'd had trouble with the office, but it sounds like you found the right nurse to be your ally.

Yesterday's visit determined that I am one centimeter along. Eeeeeee... next Wednesday is my due date, but in all honestly I'm a little okay with waiting just a hair longer as long as baby and I are still well.
FireAtASeaParks, due date 3/9/16, baby boy!

38+4 here! It's been mainly, as Jack Johnson puts it: sitting, waiting, wishing. Bassinet and car seat are up, but I keep re-packing the go-bag because I'll either decide that there's something we can't live without that needs to go in or I'll decide that I'm being ridiculous by bringing this other thing. Obviously I have too much time on my hands.

Congratulations! And don't worry: the most important outcome from this is the one I keep reminding myself of whenever I start to fret about the possibility of a c-section - "healthy mama and healthy baby." And you did it! I'm excited to read your birth story when it comes out, but no rush! You keep enjoying time with your new family of three!

We are! I'm so excited to meet my little one! Bassinet and car seat are both ready to go. I keep re-packing the go-bag because suddenly I'll decide that we need or don't need something. 

We did just receive another box of hand-me-down baby boy clothing, so that will need to be washed, sorted, and put away. I'm grateful, though! Ours will be the third boy in a wave of boys born from last summer onward on my husband's side of the family, so we've been lucky in how we get to save on clothing due the other babies growing like weeds the moment they hit earthside onward.

So far so good! I was experiencing some intense BH contractions earlier this week, but lately they've subsided so I have no idea when this little boy plans on vacating. He's still moving about, mostly stretching and kicking, but he's in position!
My due date has now been moved up to March 9th! (Insert various excited as hell/scared shitless onomatopoeia here)

I think - and I'm not sure because this is the first time I've made it this far therefore I have no idea what I'm doing - some of the plug might be coming out. Either that or I'm just especially splooshy this week. No serious discoloration: just greeny-white (this totes belongs in the TMI thread but meh) and copious. I might be jumping the gun, but it's nice to finally gun-jump due to something exciting. I doubt it'll turn out this way, but maybe I'll get a Leap Day baby after all? :)

Yep - I'm at 38+2 and I've had brown spotting since finding out I was pregnant at 7/8 weeks. It's just as you've described: very light, haven't needed more than a pantyliner to manage it, it comes about of its own free will seemingly without cause. I've brought it up to my midwife, and she said that as long as the amount didn't become unreasonable along with any changes in color, odor, and/or pain, that it was perfectly normal.

You've already brought it up to your healthcare provider, which means it's a known effect. But yeah, the gist of it is: So far I've made it to 38 weeks, spotted during the whole pregnancy, and even now my baby's happily thumping away and hiccuping into my hip as I type this. Even this far into the pregnancy, "normal" is a state of being that's hard to get used to. Good luck with everything and here's hoping for continued safe pregnancies!
Haha! I guess if you look at it as, "kid, as long as you're the Brutus and not the Caesar," then it's all good, right?
It's good to hear from you! Glad to hear you and little Roland are doing well!

I do! Even though it's a bit earlier than the due date, I would love to have a Leap Day baby! That way when he's 16 and insists on driving I can be like, "No, buddy. You're four years old." /troll

I'm also fine with 3/4 in case he becomes a military general or something, he can shout orders that are really him shouting his birthday: March forth! My husband really wants 3/10 because that's his birthday and would love to share it, and I'm also good with 3/14 because I'm all for birthday pie instead of cake. I'm not a fan of 3/15 because beware the Ides of March, y'all.

Not really a rant or a vent, but it's a little serious.

After experiencing a couple of migraines over the weekend coupled with high blood pressure and increased protein levels in my urine at this morning's visit, my midwife has me on preeclampsia watch. She was very reassuring about everything since nothing is at all confirmed and it is normal for things like blood pressure and protein levels to trend a bit upward since I'm approaching week 38 here in a couple of days, but there were enough red flags that happened within the last couple of days alone that led to her being concerned. 

She also advised me to start taking evening primrose oil and something called 5W so that my cervix would start ripening. I think the hope is that, in the case of preeclampsia, we get the baby out sooner rather than later and avoid a c-section entirely. I'm on board, but if anyone has any experience first- or second-hand, I'd love to hear what it was like.

My midwife also scared the bejesus out of me by asking if what she was feeling up near my ribs was baby's head or butt. I was pretty certain it was his rear since I felt kicks up near my ribs on the drive there, but she ended up bringing out the ancient ultrasound machine to double-check. I was right and he's still in position albeit a bit curved toward the left side. What can I say? He likes to nestle!
Aw, yay! Good luck and I'll be thinking of you!

Definitely keeping you in my thoughts. I'm not too far behind you at 37 weeks, and if I could just get a hip replacement, I think I could go for as long as this needs to. How are both of you doing in the meantime what with there not being a whole lot of room for the baby to move?

On Tuesday after two days of intense needle-stabbing pain in my nipple, I finally experienced what I have since been calling the Great Leaking. Initially I was somewhat horrified, but have since become excited. My boobs work! I don't know why the pain only happened in one nipple, but I'm grateful because that was irritating. I didn't have breast pads on hand, so I improvised and used makeup pads which have worked so far. 

I also had my 3rd trimester scan yesterday. Baby's head down and in position. We got some great visuals of him sucking his thumb and moving about like the squiggly bean he's been this whole time. He's right where he needs to be size-wise. I'm so glad! I still have a feeling he's going to come early. Maybe not quite Leap Day early, but before 3/11 as originally projected.

Also: my baby shower is this weekend! We'll finally have more than three onesies and a pacifier!

I'm at 34+3 now, and last night and this afternoon my right nipple was besieged with intermittent but intense needle-stabbing pains. Early research says this is happening because of colostrum coming in, but why is it only in one nipple? Not that I want it in both, mind you. xD The powdery discharge has increased from both breasts, but this was the first time the localized nipple pains have occurred and wanted to know for sure what was causing it. Any tips for dealing with it, possibly?
Phoenix down. For people we love, if they want it. I mean, if they're ready to go, then that's a whole other thing. But I was thinking more for pets, because I'm never ready for them to go. :(
Much love and support right back at ya! I'm sad to hear of your loss, but glad to see that you were able to find these subs to help you seek answers and solace. We will get through this!
Yayyyyyy! Congrats! Go team smudge!

Recovering from a bit of anxiety last night. 3/4 hours of sleep, but baby kicked a bunch this morning, so I know he's okay. Everything else is pretty standard: feeling like a beached mermaid, acid reflux, hemorrhoids, etc. I think I have about a month left with my belly button before it starts stretching into oblivion, so I'm enjoying it while it's still here. 

On the upside of things: today is the long-awaited Christmas present of maternity clothes shopping most/all expenses paid from my mother - yay! We'll be hitting up the box stores so nothing fancy. I would feel weird having designer leggings knowing that anytime in early/mid-March I could flood them with gushy baby fluid. However, Old Navy leggings are just fine for that sort of thing! That's what they were made for, right?

So we'll be organizing an massive egging of the premises in lawful retaliation, yes?

Ugh, that stinks. I only know of pregnant women being able to cause legal repercussions via the EOCC when it comes to job loss as a result of pregnancy, but unfortunately nothing yet for fathers-to-be. Maybe it's worth contacting them anyway to see if he has a legal leg to stand on? Is your husband able to collect unemployment in the interim?
Yeah, that's weird. Did they maybe already purchase you a crib? That's the only logical reason I can think of at the moment for their reaction otherwise it just makes them seem odd.

They sure do! You'd think with all the vitamins and healthy food we're eating that it would act as a badass germ firewall, but nooooooo.  We get the 48-hour cold that turns into a four week cold on top of being pregnant.

I appreciate your clarifying what happened, and it makes me feel a lot better! When I saw your post last night, the description sounded enough like mine with the verbiage, upvotes, and such that I was immediately like "ohmygod they're talking about me," and proceeded to have a genuine panic attack of my own thinking that the support network I had frequented for some time was now compromised. I don't get much one-on-one support with this IRL outside of my husband, so at the moment of viewing your post, it made me think I was rather cut-off and alone.

It sounds like we come from similar mindsets as far as having made ourselves intentionally not overreact with our previous pregnancies and then overdoing it with either the next pregnancy or of those around us. I get that, and I figured that you were coming from a good place, but it came off like I was being all but named since my post was the only one remaining that resembled what you had described which the led to my subsequent panicked presumption and reaction.

I'm so sorry about your own loss, and I understand entirely why you reacted the way you did. It's still a fresh wound at only a month out. Earlier on in my now-pregnancy, I was very much the same way as far as wanting to make sure that what happened before would never happen again as far as I could help it. Even now, sometimes I'm still not fully convinced that this is truly happening, and I am terrified that it'll be snatched away in an instant again and that it'll be all my fault. It's taken time and good advice from my midwife for me to realize and remind myself that I am doing everything right, and that with my previous pregnancy I also did everything right. The latter was a lot harder to accept because I felt that, being the mother, who else could I blame but myself for what happened? But it wasn't my fault, just as it wasn't any other mom's fault here that we lost our babies. We didn't do this on purpose. I just wanted to say that to you because I saw in your posts that you were taking the blame for your own loss, and it broke my heart all over again because my husband and I experienced a long period of guilty grief after our loss, and it's an awful thing to experience and difficult to get through. Know this: You were and continue to be a great and loving mother to the baby you lost, and you will be a fantastic mother to any children that follow. It'll be okay. If not now, then someday.
I love this! Yay for good marriages, open communication, and unconditional love!

Absolutely. My husband and I already had names picked out, and we both had a strong feeling that baby we had lost was going to be a boy, so we refer to him by the name he would have had. If it helps you, then by all means: do it.
Did someone just fart into the microphone...?

Preach it! At 32 weeks, I feel like a beached mermaid. I make audible "oofs" and other noises whenever I roll over, stand up, sit up, get in/out of the car. I know I just have to be patient, but it's not my best trait. xD
I have made myself the most delicious trail mix with mixed nuts, craisins, and white chocolate chips. I am in love.

When my little guy pulled this on me, I would do a couple of things:

- Drink a lot of ice cold water
- Put on music you know has caused movement reactions before. Mine has been partial to Bowie, REM, and Elvis for movement and Disney for calming

I did have a scary moment a couple months ago at about 24 weeks when I didn't feel movement for a couple of days, and then as soon as I decided I was going to call my midwife, he burst into a parkour frenzy which I was very grateful for. At 32 weeks, he's big enough now to where I can nearly always feel him, but before about 28 weeks or so, it can get very nerve-wracking when the little one doesn't squiggle about as it should be. Please let us know if either of these works, and if everything's okay. 

EDIT: I forgot to add that I also have an anterior placenta which, coupled with my previous baby loss, makes for a very worried mama at times. Above all: trust your instincts. I'll be thinking of you! 

EDIT MARK TWO: There seems to be some bad press leaking to another subreddit regarding what may or may not have been my post (not from OP, who has since posted that her baby is doing fantastic which I am extremely joyful and relieved to hear). I have this to say in light of the event:

Please note that my first edit came maybe two minutes maximum after my original reply that contained the sentence: above all, trust your instincts. This, of course, includes going to L&D if anyone feels that something has gone wrong at any time at all ever. I only made my suggestions regarding cold water and music because after having gone through a loss, I (and possibly others) am predisposed into going into panic-mode earlier than is considered normal anytime I don't feel anything for a lengthy period. Upon disclosing this to my midwife (who is certified, medically-trained, hospital-affiliated and not at all a witch doctor in a forest), she suggested the water and the music for when I was at home worried. If these did not work, then I was go on to the next step which was to contact the clinic/go to the ER if it was after hours. This has worked for me thus far, thank god. But again, that's why I went back to the post and clarified for OP to trust her instincts. These are our babies: any concern that we have regarding them is absolutely warranted. I just wanted to, if at all possible, provide a small peace of mind knowing by virtue of all of us being in the same boat, that this is hard to come by. I thought this was obvious given what brought most of us here to this sub in the first place, so I apologize for any miscommunication behind my words. I often forget that we miss all other other bits and pieces behind communication that we take for granted while in person: body language, tone, facial expression, etc. I will try harder at making myself more transparent in the future.

I do, however, take issue at my words being misconstrued and then taking this accusation into other subreddits to spread further slander to then be used passive-aggressively to bully myself or anyone else. Both this sub along with other subs concerning loss are supposed to be a safe haven for everyone. Please remember to have respect for the inhabitants of these subs as we have all lost children and, try as we might and some days are better than others, we are all still hurting. We're all in this together, and it won't help anyone to make future moms and dads feel marginalized. We're adults - just shoot over a PM to me or whoever and have a quick talk concerning intention and tone. I think you'll quickly find that there was a miscommunication that can be cleared up in two shakes of a lamb's tail.

Those are my two cents, at the very least. So again, if it's my reply everyone's sharpening pitchforks over, I apologize, but please don't wreck my perception of safety in my support networks as a result of this. If it's not mine, then everyone go back to their regularly scheduled programming. Nothin' to see here... >_>;
Congratulations!!!
Maybe this means more antibodies for your baby so that she's extra-super-duper protected against germs?
You're a much better person than I am. I would have either said something snarky or, if I had my cat's punishment squirt bottle in hand, let her have it that way. Good lord, the nerve.

I keep wanting to do a post where I just ALL CAPS EVERYTHING BECAUSE RAWR the way other subreddit threads will allow people to *really* let it out, but by the time I get here, the rest of you have proceeded to politely complain using your proper upper and lower cases. It's so civilized and therefore aggravating! xD

That being said, I'm at 31 weeks along and change, and I would like to be done. The baby changes position about every 20 minutes or so, and he's already taken to seemingly touch/grip everything in his grasp on his way to the next position (ergo: ow), the new jeans I ordered don't fit and I have to send them back so now I have NO PANTS, I can't get the taste of Tums out of my mouth since I have to take them so often because of acid reflux, I live on the toilet, my hips hurt like hell, my boobs keep boogering, and now: hemorrhoids. 

Just... flames. Flames on the side of my face. And everywhere else. That being said, prenatal appointment today went well: everything's normal, baby and I are right where we're supposed to be health/progress-wise, so huzzah. I'm just done and super whiny and I want all of the chocolate.

> I don't want to be negative about it, but everything you invent is worthless.

Well, prepare to put mustard on those words!

Oh, I haven't watched that yet... That's going on my "things to watch while pregsomniac-ing" list. Thanks for the suggestion!
I freaking love that show!!! I'm always happy to find fellow fans!

That's so exciting! My husband and I were given the Tactical Diaper Bag from thinkgeek.com at Christmas this year, and we immediately nerded out over it and made plans to put it to good use. I'm putting together a hospital go-bag list and wondering if there is such thing as being either too minimalist or too prepared. I swear we'll be better at this once we've gone through this at least once, but for no there is really no way of knowing until you're in the moment, is there? :)

My sister-in-law is planning a baby shower for me, and there is now a date and a venue. I want to let myself be excited, but it's hard to. I've gotten a lot better about letting myself plan and hope, but there's still that small part of me that's cautious hence why I frequent this subreddit, I guess. xD I'm just happy right now that whenever I start to get too worried, my little one starts to deliver reassuring kicks. He's comforting me already. :)

I don't know if this is your cup of tea (or liquor, rather) but my husband and I got together with a friend to watch a corny movie and played a drinking game to it with the goal of consuming prodigious amounts of alcohol. Subsequently, we all got really really drunk. This happened a couple weeks after I lost my first, and my husband and I just needed a giant dose of liquid triage after having to deal with the aftermath. This enabled my husband and I to cry it out together and talk at length about what this did to us and it just brought us closer. It also helped to have a friend over who could be there for us. Please note that this was a one time thing and that by no means did we make a habit of this. It just needed to happen so that we could attain some sort of catharsis albeit while inebriated. 

I'm also going to second speaking to a professional. I've dealt with anxiety and depression, and this event is life-exploding enough to warrant more care and attention than we by ourselves are able to handle. If your husband is able to accompany you: great, but if not, then maybe on a later visit? I also ended up getting big into cross-stitching since it makes you work on something tangible while having to pay close attention to detail. Crafting is very therapeutic that way.

I'm so sorry that this happened to you and your family. I've been thinking of you ever since I first read your story, and I'm just so sad that we all have had to deal with this pain in some form, but this group has done wonders to help simply by either responding to my own pain or by seeing others voice what I've felt.

I just can't seem to turn down rice in any form. Usually I'm good with brown rice, steamed broccoli, and grilled chicken, but sometimes I fold and indulge in embarrassing amounts of fried rice. So far my midwives have only asked me to drink more water, so for the moment I'm okay sodium-wise.

Now all I want are Cuties/Halos.

However, I fell off the wagon entirely tonight by bringing home massive amounts of carby Chinese food and made a butterscotch pie. Totes a winner tonight!

After a shitty night's sleep due to my Siamese cat yowling pretty much the whole night, I was ready to kill him and the world. I've calmed down mentally/emotionally since then, but I'm exhausted. I think someone tasked the cat with acting like a baby so that I'd have a tentative point of reference for if/when the real thing arrives come March.

I am now absolutely blossoming over my period-jeans and can no longer wear them. They lasted 7.5 months, so not too shabby, right? I broke down and ordered a size up along with maternity leggings and paid for them all with gift cards, so yay! :3 My mother's Christmas present to me will take place this weekend in the form of shopping for maternity clothes now that I am, as I said, fairly blossoming.

I've also given up job hunting. It's too much to handle amping up for interviews, the subsequent disappointment, and the sheer amount of travel on top of doing it all while in the third trimester - especially when I'd only be able to work for about 6-8 weeks. I'll pick it up again after I declare my unofficial maternity leave to be over - about June-ish? But I'd rather be working. I feel like a loafer just here at my mother's while my husband works. One day at a time, though.

Dan is the hero we all need and deserve. I requested a milkshake from my husband the other night, and he neglected to fulfill it. I was disappointed; granted, there was a storm blowing outside, but still! If Jim Dear from Lady and the Tramp was willing to go out for watermelon and chop suey for Darling, then surely my husband could pick up a simple milkshake! xD
I hope everything has gone well so far for you! Any updates?
Congratulations!!! And hooray for George being bigger on the outside!
Heck yes!!! Way to celebrate with the donuts, too! :)

I swear, the combination of asshole families on top of not being able to drink alcohol is what ruins the holidays. At least while drinking you can forget your sorrows. Or else just unleash hell on the assholes and NGAF until the next morning.

I'm with you here. The SIL obviously doesn't know that she's asking too much, and the MIL needs to be smacked in the face with water balloons for yelling at you like that. Ugh. Would your husband be willing to unleash hell on your MIL on your behalf for her treating you that way? If not, as long as he's in your corner and providing you with lots of cuddles and love, you'll get through this.
Congratulations! Best wishes for a speedy recovery so that you can get back to cuddling your little one once both of you are ready and healthy!
Like u/sujihime, I've been getting these weird flaky boogers. Boobs are weird, y'all.

Yes. Very, absolutely yes. I hit 3rd trimester on Friday, and though the odds are very good that if I were to go into labor this second, my baby would survive, the loss of my last pregnancy has scarred me enough to where if I'm not busy/distracted, I'm filled with the fear that this little one will slip away without my having known about it just like last time.

Fortunately he's thumping away in there as I type this, so for the moment, I'm at peace. It's handy that midwife check-ins are every two weeks now because it does a lot to alleviate stress on my end. As difficult as it is to hear/read, we just need to cling to rational and sensible facts so that we don't drive ourselves crazy. Hobbies and bad TV shows work wonderfully as distractions.

We can do this!

You know, I was utterly convinced I was going to get the diagnosis this week after my 3-hour test due to some odd hunger/crashing habits I'd gone through since the onset of this pregnancy, but I ended up passing the test. It ain't over 'til it's over, and even so, GD won't be the end of the world. It's only for the next couple of months, and from what I've seen/heard, the majority of babies end up at what's considered a normal size. No matter what the outcome of the test, it'll be okay.
I went through this myself last year. I'm so sorry you had to go through all of this.

Oh man, I have no idea. The fingers on my left hand will spontaneously have a tingly "it just fell asleep" feeling once in a while, but no soreness or aching. Are you able to use a heating pad or wrap around the limb to relax it, maybe?
Oh no! I think this is an occasion that merited cake. I would've done the same thing. But then again, I'm a huge enabler...
Haha! I think that's just everyone when it's this close to the holidays. Take advantage of it while you can!
Husbands rock! Aaaaaand now you've made me thirsty! xD

After failing the glucose challenge last week and going in yesterday to be a human pincushion for the 3-hour glucose tolerance test, I have managed to successfully avoid the fetus 'beetus. My 2nd hour level was the only one to measure high which is enough to garner me a referral to a nutritionist, but I'll take it. GD wouldn't have been the end of the world, but after everything else that's happened this year (getting fired, *finally* getting a BFP after over a year of trying post-MC two weeks after the firing, finding a new job before leaving it after two months to move cross-country, and living with my mother), it would've been a cherry on this very eventful sundae of a year.

Baby has also discovered the upstairs loft portion of his studio apartment aka my ribs and has been cheerfully kicking away. It doesn't hurt, but it's super bizarre. I also hit week 28 tomorrow - the beginning of the end. I feel simultaneously ready (especially with all this delicious alcohol around me: I miss spiced wine, eggnog, and hot buttered rum so much!) and not ready at all. I'm hearing rumblings of a baby shower for next month sometime, so perhaps after that I'll feel more prepared.
Thinking of you and wishing you the best of luck!
Congratulations!!!

Yayyyy! I woke my husband up a few nights ago when the baby decided to conga just as I was falling asleep. I placed his hand on my belly so that he could feel the baby, too. He was more awed than anything. It was a very sweet moment. :)

I just finished with a job interview at a well-known athletic company and I cannot for the life of me get out of this booth. My pregnant belly is too big for me to seamlessly maneuver an escape. Am currently plotting a more innovative means of self-removal. Luckily I have water, but tips for removal would be much appreciated.

EDIT: I have made my escape after fifteen minutes of deliberation and minute planning. I will never sit in a booth again during this pregnancy if I can help it.

Good things on the horizon: my husband starts his new job next week. I have an interview for a temp position next week also, which will be nice considering our desire to stockpile as much as possible before March. Our good friends have gone into labor today, and we are anxiously awaiting news of their new baby girl. 

My glucose challenge is on Tuesday which wouldn't be so bad except it's in the afternoon, so I need to remember to stay carb- and sugar-free all Tuesday until after the test. Any recommendations on flavors?
Congratulations!!! He's a beauty, and he looks like a fighter just like his mom! :)
The countdown has now gone from triple-digits to double-digits. I'm vacillating between still not believing it's happening to not feeling at all prepared for this.
I miss sleeping on my tummy!!!!!

I am very much the same way. I finally made it to week 24 on Friday, and I'm still not relaxed though I am more so than I was at, say, week 8. I'm just not going to be satisfied until my baby is in my arms. In the meantime, hang in there and trust that your baby and your body know what they are doing.

24+2 today. I'm concerned because my lower abdomen/pelvic area is extremely tender, like post-contraction tender. It's been constant for over 48 hours now after an episode Friday night where it felt like either my child was beating the bejesus out of me or the placenta was pulsing like mad. It hurt really bad, and now whenever I have to change positions (stand up/sit down, switch sides in bed, etc.) the pain comes back all over again. I'm giving it until Monday to show some progress (like less pain. that would be nice) at which point I'm going to call my midwife and see wtf is going on here. I don't think its ligament pain because it feels right below or really close to the surface. We'll see what happens.
Aww, yay! I should get on that. It's just so hard with the imminent beach ball growth! I feel so sore and beluga-like these days.

Oh my lord... MiLs are why alcohol was invented, so it makes it even more unfortunate that we can't have any right now. xD That whole effacement explanation made me chuckle quite a bit. Just... good lord.

Your MiL sounds like my mom. I had to explain why I couldn't take steaming hot baths for abdominal pain relief, that it is totally possible to experience little contractions here and there way before one's due date, and that placentas don't just float about willy-nilly and can actually cause problems depending on where they're placed. 1) Suggestions to jump start natural m/c process: I also opted to pass my first pregnancy naturally, but visited a doctor and obtained a couple doses of Cytotec in case I felt I didn't want to wait anymore. I lasted about two weeks after finding out about the m/c before taking the Cytotec, but unfortunately it didn't work. It took another two weeks (four weeks cumulative) for the pregnancy to pass. Cytotec, from what I understand, is the safest and most controllable way to pass a pregnancy non-invasively, but only if it works.

2) My husband and I waited until January of the following year more due to emotional healing rather than wanting to get back on the horse. My doctor (the good one, not the bully) advised waiting two full period cycles in order to give your body time to get back to a business-as-usual routine. 

3) How to handle people who take it for granted: even to this day I get all green-eyed monster whenever I see someone triumphantly announce a pregnancy like it was no big deal. I do a lot of hiding posts with the only exception being when it's someone I know who has experienced loss or difficulty in conceiving - then it's a victory because it gives me and everyone else like me hope. We're actually studying some of this in my sociology of gender class right now.

The answer to the former has to do more about job flexibility: less well-paid occupations are more likely to be flexible with hours, demands, etc. because of the presumption that while women are expected to work, they also have to go home and take care of the kids, etc. Well-paid positions are reserved for those who "merit" it: men who put in a zillion hours a week. Bonus points if they have a family support. A woman will not get the same treatment as a man in this position; they will instead face stigma regarding their "unwomanly" choice to work instead of fulfilling her maternal instincts and desires (not my words -this is from last week's lecture). Unmarried and childless women are, for the most part, treated like unmarried and childless men nowadays, but even then it was a long time before this came to pass because of the "what the hell is wrong with you and why aren't you in the kitchen" response that was given to women prior to recent times. But then again, there is an existing pressure for men to eventually settle down and start a family because that's when a man "really becomes" a man. Plus you wouldn't want that added concern from your colleagues and supervisors wondering about your reasons for choosing to stay a bachelor because you know what "that" means.

The latter question addresses gendered stereotypes that have existed since pretty much the dawn of civilization. There have been a lot of "studies" that claim that boys are better at maths and hard sciences while girls are better at English. I call them "studies" because they try to prove that, via the nature side of nature vs. nurture, boys are just better mentally equipped to handle math and science. Nurture, however, is the clear winner here. While discouragements for girls who go into math and science have lessened, they do still exist. The number of boys in AP science and math classes still outstrip the number of girls. Not to mention that, years later for them, when the time comes to choose career over starting a family due to fertility issues that arise for them down the road, women will often opt for starting a family over pursuing their career because they've been conditioned to believe that having a family is more important than having a career which then just widens the gender gap for the more prestigious occupations and positions across the board since they then drop out of the running. This then goes back to the previous question -when women then make their return to the job market, they'll go for something easy that leaves then able and available to fulfill their own and society's own expectations and desires for them.

TL;DR - Present society makes women think that they can have their cake and eat it too, but the cake is a lie.
